title: Query Plan Regressions: Parameter Sniffing & Generic vs Custom Plans
realWorldScenario: A prepared statement `SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = $1` runs in 0.8ms for the first 4 executions. On the 5th execution, latency explodes to 1,400ms and remains permanently slow for all subsequent queries.
questionStatement: Explain PostgreSQL prepared statement execution planning. What is the difference between a Custom Plan and a Generic Plan? How does the 5-execution threshold trigger plan caching, why does parameter sniffing cause plan regressions on skewed data, and how do you fix it?
expectedConcepts: Custom Plan (parameter substitution) vs Generic Plan ($1 placeholder)
5-execution comparison threshold in PostgreSQL driver protocol
Data distribution skew (e.g. 98% vs 0.1%) breaking generic plans
Disabling prepared statement caching for skewed filter columns
hints: Why does PostgreSQL test the query 5 times before making a permanent plan decision?
What happens when 98% of rows have status "DELIVERED" and 0.1% have "PENDING"?
